JEE Main Mathematics, Unit 14: Trigonometry: Teacher bank

160 questions · four options, one correct · marking +4 / −1 / 0. Difficulty labels are editorial estimates. Unless a question says otherwise: log without a base and loge denote the natural logarithm; arguments of complex numbers are principal values in (−π, π]; inverse trigonometric functions take principal values. Syllabus basis: NTA JEE Main 2026.

Includes keys, worked solutions, targeted misconceptions and numerical-answer forms.

JEE-MATH-U14-001 · Unit 14: Trigonometry · Trigonometric identities · Easy · Class XI
The value of sin275∘−sin215∘ is
  1. (A)1
  2. (B)43​​
  3. (C)21​
  4. (D)23​​
Answer and solution

Answer: (D) 23​​

Using sin2A−sin2B=sin(A+B)sin(A−B), the value is sin90∘sin60∘=23​​. Equivalently sin275∘−sin215∘=cos215∘−sin215∘=cos30∘.

Targets: Confusing a2−b2 with (a−b)2 when a,b are trigonometric values.
Difficulty: One standard identity applied once.
Family: U14-A-sin-square-difference · Check: MACHINE_RECOMPUTED; BLIND_RESOLVED; EDITORIAL_AUDITED; ERRATA_RECOMPUTED; ERRATA_AUDITED

JEE-MATH-U14-002 · Unit 14: Trigonometry · Trigonometric identities · Easy · Class XI
The value of tan75∘−tan15∘ is
  1. (A)23​​
  2. (B)3​
  3. (C)23​
  4. (D)4
Answer and solution

Answer: (C) 23​

tan75∘−tan15∘=cos75∘cos15∘sin60∘​ and cos75∘cos15∘=21​(cos90∘+cos60∘)=41​. Hence the value is 1/43​/2​=23​ (also (2+3​)−(2−3​)=23​).

Targets: Treating tanA−tanB as tan(A−B).
Difficulty: Two special values, or one identity, in one or two steps.
Family: U14-A-tan75-tan15 · Check: MACHINE_RECOMPUTED; BLIND_RESOLVED; EDITORIAL_AUDITED; ERRATA_RECOMPUTED; ERRATA_AUDITED

JEE-MATH-U14-003 · Unit 14: Trigonometry · Trigonometric identities · Easy · Class XI
The value of cos36∘−cos72∘ is
  1. (A)21​
  2. (B)25​​
  3. (C)41​

Answer and solution

Answer: (A) 21​

cos36∘=45​+1​ and cos72∘=sin18∘=45​−1​, so the difference is 42​=21​.

JEE-MATH-U14-004 · Unit 14: Trigonometry · Trigonometric identities · Easy · Class XI

  1. (A)197​
  2. (B)59​
  3. (C)21​
  4. (D)139​
Answer and solution

Answer: (D) 139​

tan2A=1−41​2⋅21​​=34​. Then tan(2A−B)=1+34​⋅31​34​−31​​=13/91​=139​.

JEE-MATH-U14-007 · Unit 14: Trigonometry · Trigonometric identities · Easy · Class XI
The value of sin210∘+sin220∘+sin230∘+⋯+sin290∘ (angles increasing in steps of 10∘) is
  1. (A)211​
  2. (B)5
  3. (C)4
  4. (D)29​
Answer and solution

Answer: (B) 5

Since sin2(90∘−θ)=cos2θ, the pairs (10∘,80∘),(20∘,70∘),(30∘,60∘),(40∘,50∘) each contribute 1. Adding sin290∘=1 gives 4+1=5.

  1. (A)tan6x

  1. (A)−tanB
  2. (B)tan2B​

sinB1−cosB​=2sin(B/2)cos(B/2)2sin2(B/2)​=tan2B​. So tanA=tan2B​ and tan2A=1−tan2(B/2)2tan(B/2)​=tanB.

JEE-MATH-U14-020 · Unit 14: Trigonometry · Trigonometric identities · Medium · Class XI
If A, B, C are the angles of a triangle, then sinAsinBsinCsin2A+sin2B+sin2C​ equals
  1. (A)2
  2. (B)6
  3. (C)4

Answer and solution

Answer: (C) 4

sin2A+sin2B=2sin(A+B)cos(A−B)=2sinCcos(A−B) and sin2C=2sinCcosC=−2sinCcos(A+B). So the numerator is 2sinC[cos(A−B)−cos(A+B)]=4sinAsinBsinC, and the ratio is 4.

JEE-MATH-U14-022 · Unit 14: Trigonometry · Trigonometric identities · Medium · Class XI
Let A+B+C=π. Statement I: cos2A+cos2B+cos2C+2cosAcosBcosC=1. Statement II: sin2A+sin2B+sin2C=2−2cosAcosBcosC. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer.
  1. (A)Statement I is true but Statement II is false
  2. (B)Statement I is false but Statement II is true
  3. (C)Both Statement I and Statement II are true
  4. (D)Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Answer and solution

Answer: (A) Statement I is true but Statement II is false

Statement I: cos2A+cos2B=1+cos(A+B)cos(A−B)=1−cosCcos(A−B), so cos2A+cos2B+cos2C=1−cosC[cos(A−B)+cos(A+B)]=1−2cosAcosBcosC; Statement I is true. Then sin2A+sin2B+sin2C=3−(1−2cosAcosBcosC)=2+2cosAcosBcosC, so Statement II is false (for example A=B=C=3π​ gives 49​=47​).

Targets: Sign errors when converting the cosine identity to sines.
Difficulty: Two conditional identities to verify, with a sign trap.
Family: U14-A-pi-squares-statement · Check: MACHINE_RECOMPUTED; BLIND_RESOLVED; EDITORIAL_AUDITED; ERRATA_RECOMPUTED; ERRATA_AUDITED

JEE-MATH-U14-026 · Unit 14: Trigonometry · Trigonometric identities · Medium · Class XI
If (1+tan1∘)(1+tan2∘)(1+tan3∘)⋯(1+tan45∘)=2n, then n equals
  1. (A)44
  2. (B)45
  3. (C)23
  4. (D)22
Answer and solution

Answer: (C) 23

If A+B=45∘, then tanA+tanB=1−tanAtanB, so (1+tanA)(1+tanB)=1+tanA+tanB+tanAtanB=2. The 44 factors for 1∘ to 44∘ form 22 such pairs, giving 222, and 1+tan45∘=2. So the product is 223 and n=23.

JEE-MATH-U14-029 · Unit 14: Trigonometry · Trigonometric identities · Medium · Class XI
If cos(α+β)=54​ and sin(α−β)=135​, where 0<α,β<4π​, then tan2α equals
  1. (A)6316​

Answer and solution

Answer: (B) 12π

sin2x​ has period 1/22π​=4π and cos3x​ has period 6π. Since the two terms have different frequencies, any period of the sum must be a common period of both terms, i.e. a common multiple of 4π and 6π. The least such value is LCM(4π,6π)=12π, and 12π clearly works.

The left side is at most 2⋅1⋅1=2, and the right side is at least 2 (AM-GM), with equality only at x=1. A solution would need both sides equal to 2, hence x=1; but at x=1 the left side is 2cos221​sin21<2. So there are no solutions.

JEE-MATH-U14-110 · Unit 14: Trigonometry · Signs and comparison of trigonometric values · Difficult · Class XI
For 0<x<4π​, let p=(sinx)sinx, q=(sinx)cosx and r=(cosx)sinx. Then
  1. (A)r<p<q
  2. (B)p<q<r
  3. (C)q<r<p
  4. (D)q<p<r
Answer and solution

Answer: (D) q<p<r

For 0<x<4π​, 0<sinx<cosx<1. With base sinx<1, a larger exponent gives a smaller power, so (sinx)cosx<(sinx)sinx, i.e. q<p. With the same positive exponent sinx, the larger base gives the larger power, so (sinx)sinx<(cosx)sinx, i.e. p<r. Hence q<p<r.
